entities.summary:
Gongmin, known by his Mongolian name Bayan Temür, was the 31st ruler of Goryeo, reigning from 1351 until his death on November 4, 1374. Ascending the throne amidst the declining power of the Yuan Dynasty, which had dominated Goryeo for nearly a century, Gongmin initiated a radical program of anti-Yuan reforms aimed at reasserting Goryeo's national sovereignty and cultural identity. His reign represents a pivotal, albeit ultimately tragic, period in Korean history, marking a determined effort to break free from foreign suzerainty and reclaim national autonomy, setting the stage for subsequent political transformations.

Upon his ascension, Gongmin immediately purged pro-Yuan officials and institutions, including the powerful Darughachi system imposed by the Mongols. He abolished the Ssangseong Prefectures, a Yuan-controlled territory in the northeast, and reclaimed lost lands, notably expanding Goryeo's northern frontier. He also implemented significant land reforms, attempting to curb the power of the landed aristocracy and redistribute land to the common people, and reformed the military. Crucially, he promoted meritocracy by empowering officials from the Shin Jin Sa Dae-bu (newly emerging literati-officials) class, many of whom were proponents of Neo-Confucianism and later became architects of the Joseon Dynasty.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gongmin's reign marked a critical, albeit ultimately unsuccessful, effort to restore Goryeo's sovereignty and national identity after a century of Yuan domination, influencing subsequent political developments and the eventual rise of the Joseon Dynasty. His reforms, though incomplete, highlighted deep-seated issues and inspired later transformative changes.
